archetype.name: Fringe Contender (shootout offense)
archetype.definition: Dallas has a top-five passing offense strong enough to win any week, and a bottom-ranked defense bad enough to lose any week, which leaves a .500-type team in a division nobody has taken yet.

report.headline: Same team as 2025: Dak's elite passing, the league's worst defense, coin-flip results
report.take:
This is the 2025 Cowboys again, almost number for number. Last year Dallas ranked 5th in offensive EPA and 32nd in defensive EPA. Through five games this year it is 4th and 32nd. The scoreboard shows it: 27.6 points scored a game, 27.2 allowed, a +2 point differential overall. The 2-3 record is roughly what that profile earns, maybe a hair unlucky. They are 1-3 in one-score games, and the model has them 0.88 wins below expectation. Neither number is big enough to call this a buried good team.

The offense runs through Dak Prescott's arm. He has started every game and has 1,381 yards (276 a game), and the passing EPA of 0.244 ranks 4th. The odd part is protection. Dallas allows pressure on 24.6% of dropbacks (31st) and holds the ball among the longest in the league, yet the sack rate is 2nd-best at 2.8%. Prescott is taking the pressure and getting rid of the ball anyway. The run game looks bad by yards per carry (3.42, 26th), but its 43.6% success rate ranks 8th. Javonte Williams keeps the offense on schedule even if he rarely breaks one.

The defense is the problem, and it isn't a fluke after two straight years at the bottom. The 227 passing yards allowed per game (12th) flatter it badly. Offenses aren't beating Dallas over the top so much as picking it apart underneath: EPA allowed on short passes ranks dead last, opponents convert 52.6% of third downs (32nd), and success rate allowed is also last. The pass rush generates pressure (10th) but doesn't finish, with 5 sacks and a QB hit rate 29th in the league. With only 2 takeaways, drives keep going, which is why Dallas ranks 31st in time of possession despite an efficient offense. The -0.6 turnover margin matches last season's exactly, so it's at least partly structural. A defense that creates nothing combined with an aggressive passer is a repeatable recipe.

The Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay was the ugly version. On four days' rest, the 27th-ranked offense ran for 241 yards against them, and Prescott turned it over three times as a 9.5-point favorite. That looks more like a short-week outlier than a new floor, but it shows how thin the margin is. The good news is the schedule. Eight of the eleven remaining opponents rank 15th or worse in offensive EPA, Philadelphia twice among them, and the NFC East leader is a 3-1-1 Giants team Dallas still gets at home. This defense won't be fixed, but it will face worse offenses, and that is a path to nine wins.

strengths.title: Prescott's passing game is elite
strengths.body: Dallas ranks 4th in passing EPA and 4th in overall success rate, and has scored 31+ in three of five games. It matches last year's 5th-ranked offense, so this is an established identity, not a hot start. As long as Prescott and the top two receivers stay healthy, it should hold.

strengths.title: Sacks avoided despite constant pressure
strengths.body: The line allows the 2nd-most pressure in the league, yet Dallas has given up only six sacks, a 2.8% rate. Prescott is absorbing pressure and still getting throws off. That depends on him more than the line, which makes it sturdier than it looks but leaves it exposed to injury. Losing starting tackle Tyler Guyton, questionable with a back injury, would test it.

strengths.title: Run game stays on schedule
strengths.body: The 3.42 yards per carry looks poor, but Dallas wins 43.6% of its runs, 8th in the league, and rushing EPA ranks 10th. It isn't explosive, but it keeps the play-action passing game in favorable downs, and that is all this offense needs from it.

concerns.title: Worst pass defense, second straight year
concerns.body: Dallas allows 0.382 EPA per dropback, last in the league, after also ranking last in total defensive EPA in 2025. The damage comes on short throws and third downs, not just big plays, which points to coverage and tackling rather than bad luck. With two corners on the latest injury report as out, it won't get better soon.

concerns.title: Pressure that never turns into plays
concerns.body: Dallas pressures quarterbacks at a 10th-ranked rate but has just 5 sacks and 2 takeaways, both 30th. That combination keeps opposing drives alive and puts the scoring load back on Prescott. Some regression toward more sacks is plausible, but last year's matching -0.6 turnover margin says the shortage of takeaways is partly who this defense is.

concerns.title: Run defense can be run over
concerns.body: Opponents average close to 170 rushing yards a game, and Tampa Bay's weak offense ran for 241 in Week 5. Per play the rush defense is only middling (21st in EPA allowed), so this is partly volume from a defense that can't get off the field. Still, it was a real collapse on a short week.

trend.note: The profile hasn't moved: four straight games of positive passing EPA and 20+ points, with the defense leaking every week. Week 5 against Tampa Bay was the exception on offense, with three turnovers on a four-day turnaround, rather than the start of a slide.

nextGame.headline: Rested Dallas offense meets a depleted Packers front, if the wind allows
nextGame.body:
Green Bay is a 3-2 team with a negative point differential that has won every one-score game and covered only one of four. Its offense is average (17th) and has the league's worst run game by EPA, which matters because it lets the worst run defense in the matchup off the hook. Love will throw into the league's leakiest pass defense. The Packers' defense is opportunistic, 3rd in takeaways with 14 sacks, and it rarely allows explosive passes. It has given ground underneath, though, allowing 81.3% red-zone touchdowns (31st) and gaining nothing on third downs (25th). Dallas's 10 days of rest after the Thursday game is a real edge.

Availability cuts both ways. Dallas is down corners Cobie Durant and Joey Porter Jr. and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, all listed out on the latest report, which strips a bottom-ranked secondary further. CeeDee Lamb (quad bruise, described as not serious) and starting tackle Tyler Guyton (negative back X-rays) are questionable. Green Bay's list is longer and hits the trenches: center Jacob Monk and guard Aaron Banks are out, linebacker Edgerrin Cooper and DT Javon Hargrave are lost to Achilles injuries, and Micah Parsons isn't expected back. The early forecast calls for 19 mph wind with gusts near 39, more than five days out. If that holds it hurts both passing games and the kickers, but it is too early to bank on.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against Green Bay's WR1 leak
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay has let opposing WR1s score 4.8 PPR points a game over their average (26th) while shutting down WR2s. If Lamb plays, he is the target the defense struggles with most. If he sits, George Pickens moves into a role this defense handles well.

keyMatchups.title: Ball security against a ballhawking defense
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay has nine takeaways, 3rd-most, and Dallas just turned it over three times against Tampa Bay. Prescott's aggressiveness is the engine of this offense, but in a game priced near a pick'em a negative turnover margin likely decides it.

keyMatchups.title: Packers' broken run game, thinner line
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay's rushing EPA is -0.333, last by a wide margin, and it is now without its starting center and a guard. Dallas's weakness against the run gets less exposure here. The Packers will have to win through Love's arm, which is where Dallas is weakest.

nextGame.watch: The kickoff wind forecast and Lamb's status: a calm day with Lamb active favors Dallas's passing edge, while a gusty day without him turns this into a turnover coin flip.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense should keep scoring in the mid-to-high 20s. It is the same unit that finished 5th last year, Prescott is healthy, and the low sack rate holds up across five games. The defense won't improve much in talent, and its corner injuries make the next few weeks worse. But the schedule gets much easier: Philadelphia twice (29th in offense), Tennessee, Indiana, Arizona, Seattle's weak offense and a home game against the Giants. Points allowed should drift down toward the mid-20s on opponent quality alone.

The 1-3 record in close games should even out somewhat, while the turnover deficit looks closer to real. Expect a team that goes about 6-5 or 7-5 the rest of the way and stays in the NFC East race into December, with SF, JAX, SEA and LA as the likely losses and the division games deciding it.
swingFactors: Turnover margin and Prescott's ball security

bets.reason: Green Bay's 3-2 record rests on a perfect one-score record and a negative point differential. Its offense has the league's worst run game and is now missing its starting center and a guard, while Dallas comes in on 10 days' rest with a top-five passing offense. Dallas's secondary injuries keep this from being a stronger play.

Green Bay's games have averaged about 43 total points and its offense scores 20.8 a game, so 52.5 leans on Dallas's shootout history. The Packers also allow very few explosive passes. An early forecast of 19 mph wind with near-39 mph gusts would push further toward the under if it holds.

confidence.note: Only five games, but the profile closely matches 2025, and key injuries on both sides add noise.
